subtopics.title: The Elasticity Number — Definition and Calculation

questions.question: Price elasticity of demand equals:
options: Percentage change in price divided by percentage change in quantity demanded
Percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
Change in quantity times change in price

questions.question: The taxi fare rises from R20 to R24. The percentage change in price is:
Price rises 20% and quantity demanded falls 5%. The elasticity (absolute value) is:
Strictly, elasticity of demand calculations give a negative answer because:
options: Sellers lose money when prices change
The original value goes on the bottom
Demand slopes downward, so price and quantity change in opposite directions

subtopics.title: Reading the Number — Five Categories and Their Graphs in Words

questions.question: An elasticity of 1,5 means demand is:
A perfectly inelastic demand curve appears as:
options: A vertical line — the same quantity bought at any price
A horizontal line at one price
A downward slope through the origin

questions.question: The horizontal demand line facing one small farmer in a perfectly competitive market represents elasticity of:
The lesson's warning about slope says:
options: Elasticity changes along a straight demand curve, so shape alone cannot fix the elasticity

subtopics.title: What Makes Demand Elastic or Inelastic — the Determinants

questions.question: The mightiest determinant of elasticity is:
Demand for petrol is inelastic in the week after a price jump but more elastic after a year because:
options: Time lets buyers adjust — lift clubs, smaller cars, moving closer to work
Petrol becomes a luxury over time

questions.question: A box of matches doubling in price causes almost no demand response because:
options: It claims a tiny share of the buyer's income

questions.question: Food as a whole is deeply inelastic, but one brand of bread is highly elastic. This shows that:
options: The narrower the definition of the good, the more substitutes exist and the higher the elasticity
Brands cannot be analysed with elasticity
Broad categories always have high elasticity

subtopics.title: Elasticity and Total Revenue — the Payoff

questions.question: After the fare rise, taxi revenue moved from R20 000 to:
When demand is ELASTIC, raising the price causes total revenue to:
options: Fall — the fleeing buyers outweigh the higher price per unit

questions.question: At unitary elasticity, a small price change leaves total revenue:
options: Unchanged — revenue is at its peak

questions.question: Treasury taxes cigarettes and fuel heavily because their demand is:
options: Inelastic, so buyers stay and tax revenue flows reliably

subtopics.title: The Shrug Test — Ouch Alone Is Not the Question

questions.question: Elasticity measures:
options: How much buyers complain about a price rise
What buyers DO when the price changes
How much profit a firm makes

questions.question: In the lesson's language, bread is a 'plank' because:
options: Push its price and buying hardly bends

questions.question: Price up 20%, purchases down 30%. Dividing buying-change by price-change gives:

subtopics.title: Why Bread Is a Plank and Cooldrink Is a Rubber Band

questions.question: The 'escape route' question is really asking about:
options: Substitutes — whether buyers can switch to something else

questions.question: Which good is most likely a 'plank' for a commuting worker with no bus or train option?
Cigarettes stay heavily bought through every price rise mainly because:
options: Addiction blocks the escape route from inside the buyer
They are a tiny share of any budget

questions.question: Time affects elasticity by:
options: Slowly turning planks into rubber bands as buyers find ways to adjust

subtopics.title: The Shopkeeper's Dilemma — When Raising the Price Loses You Money

questions.question: Mama Dee's airtime price rise GREW her revenue because airtime at school is:
options: A rubber band with many substitutes
A plank — buyers stayed and paid more per sale

questions.question: Her chocolate revenue after the price rise was:
For a rubber-band good, a price CUT can grow revenue because:
options: The flood of new buyers outweighs the discount per unit
Revenue always rises when prices move

questions.question: VAT stays off brown bread and maize meal because taxing the poor's planks would:
options: Squeeze hardest exactly where buyers cannot cut back
